Welcome to the PRIDE Academy
I am thrilled to be working with everyone in our community, and look forward to seeing us all triumph with perseverance.

Ethos and Values
The aim is for our young people to lead a happy and holistically prosperous life by developing the skills for them to move successfully along their life journeys. This includes academic outcomes that reflects the best of their abilities, being able to sustain relationships and employment and maintaining healthy households.
The PRIDE Academy follows a reflective and restorative approach with students, as opposed to for or to them. This allows staff and students to work collaboratively in a solution focused thinking manner.
The common thread throughout the school is based on 3 reflective questions:
Where are we? – our current attainment, the work we have completed, in our performance targets
What have we tried? – our achievements so far, things that are working
How do we move forward? – our next actions, targets and goals
Values
We value our PRIDE principles and strongly align these with our BRITISH VALUES (Rule of Law, Democracy, Mutual Respect and Individual Liberty):
Perseverance – we keep trying, no matter what
Respect –we show consideration to each other, our building and our community
Integrity – we are honest and fair
Diversity – we recognise our individual differences
Empathy – we notice, understand and share the emotions of others

Whilst at The PRIDE Academy, students learn the skills and attitudes required to enable them to become as independent as they can be and to prepare for adulthood. We aim for students to have an enriched and stimulating curriculum to give them every opportunity to reach their full potential.

We are always looking for additional opportunities to inspire and educate our students about the world of work. If you think you could help please contact info@theprideacademy.co.uk

Our Careers Programme lists some of the elements of careers information, advice and guidance that a student will encounter during their time with us. The careers programme is reviewed annually.

Personal Development
Personal Development Programme
The Pride Academy have introduced the Personal Development programme as a key curriculum area. The Five Pillars of Personal Development provide an overview of the skills covered which aim to enhance the curriculum offer and extend beyond the academic by providing broad and varied activities for students to participate in. To build on the success of enrichment sessions last year we have listened to student voice to increase the breadth of experiences that students are able to encounter.
Personal development sessions are part of the daily timetable where students can gain new skills and knowledge whilst fostering existing interests and passions. These sessions provide students with opportunities to engage positively with the wider community, support and promote their independence and become responsible active citizens who contribute positively to society.
Students can sign up for six-week periods and work towards achieving AQA unit awards, Duke of Edinburgh skills evidence and Sports Leaders/Dance Leaders qualifications in a range of diverse on- and off-site activities that seek to develop their social, physical, creative, digital, and cultural skills.
Personal development sessions aim to strengthen and develop peer relationships through collaborative learning experiences which bring students together irrespective of age, disability, race, or beliefs. As a whole school objective, we strive to develop student character, equipping them with skills to communicate effectively, reflect wisely, learn eagerly, and behave with integrity. Sessions will promote students’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development as well as building an awareness of Fundamental British Values such as democracy, individual liberty, rule of law, respect and tolerance. Physical development recognises the importance of leading healthy and active lives and provides students with tools to understand how to maintain positive physical and mental wellbeing.
Personal Development sessions are offered to all students in years 7 -13 with a primary aim to build independence, resilience and character. Content is delivered through personalised instruction that addresses students’ visual, auditory, and kinaesthetic learning styles, serving to motivate and inspire students to immerse themselves in their chosen activities.
Our curriculum principles are woven into the extensive personal development offer, ensuring that sessions contribute to a broad and ambitious, personalised, culturally rich curriculum that serves to prepare students for adulthood.

pageCache.pageTitle: Students Explore Careers at Hilton Heathrow Terminal 4 - Pride Academy
pageCache.text:
Students recently enjoyed a hands-on careers experience at the Hilton London Heathrow Airport Terminal 4 during a special “takeover day” designed to give them a real insight into working in the hospitality industry. Throughout the day, students took part in a range of practical activities across the hotel, helping them explore the wide variety of career opportunities available within hotels and hospitality.
One of the first challenges was learning how to make a bed “the Hilton way”. Something students quickly discovered was much trickier than it looked. Attention to detail, presentation and teamwork were all key skills they experienced first-hand.
Students also spent time outside with planting and gardening tasks, making the most of the sunny weather while learning more about maintaining professional outdoor spaces and creating a welcoming environment for guests.
Another highlight of the day was mocktail making, where students enjoyed creating and serving their own drinks before getting to taste the finished results themselves. They also practised setting formal dinner tables, carefully learning where each piece of cutlery and tableware should be placed and why presentation is such an important part of the guest experience.
To finish the day, students tried their hand at towel art, creating decorative towel displays often seen in hotels around the world.
The visit gave students a valuable opportunity to experience the fast-paced and varied nature of the hospitality sector while building confidence, communication skills and independence in a real working environment.
Staff said students were incredibly appreciative of the opportunity and gained a much greater understanding of the different roles involved in running a successful hotel. A huge thank you goes to the team at Hilton London Heathrow Airport Terminal 4 for welcoming our students and providing such an engaging and memorable experience.

Equality & Diversity
The PRIDE Academy is committed to creating an inclusive environment, where people are treated with dignity and respect and where we anticipate and respond positively to different needs and circumstances so that everyone can achieve their potential.
We are committed to promoting and advancing equality of opportunity, not only because it is an important part of the mission, vision and values of the Academy, but also because by attracting and retaining the most diverse range of students, staff and partners, we will ensure the Academy’s future success.
We believe that everyone has the right to be treated fairly and without discrimination, regardless of their circumstances or background and to be appreciated for their genuine self. In particular we make sure that all our policies and practice prevent discrimination against someone on the grounds of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.
We will consult and involve the school community in our decision making.

Free School
The PRIDE Academy is a Free School. It is a co-educational special school with 110 places for children and young people aged 11-19 (which includes 20 Sixth Form places) who have social, emotional and mental health difficulties (SEMH) in association with a range of learning needs, including a high proportion with Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in the Hillingdon and North West London region.
The school is based in a brand new, purpose-built school and opened in April 2022.
Formerly known as the Young People’s Academy, the school is based in the London Borough of Hillingdon, and provided places for children and young people from the ages of 11-16. The new Free School, extends the provision in the area from Key Stage 3 through to post 16.
We strongly believe that extending entry in this way will support children to achieve more fully as a result of access to specialist intervention and teaching continuously through to post 16. This extended age range and increased numbers presents a substantial change in the profile of our existing facilities.
About Orchard Hill College Academy Trust
The PRIDE Academy will be an important part of an established family of specialist schools and academies that make up Orchard Hill College Academy Trust (OHCAT). OHCAT is a ‘family ‘of schools, currently comprised of 13 special academies across London, Surrey, Sussex and Berkshire.
OHCAT was established in 2013 by Orchard Hill College (OHC) to share its expertise and provide services and support to specialist schools. Together, Orchard Hill College & Academy Trust (OHC&AT) provides for over 2000 pupils and students from nursery through to further education and into adulthood.
All of us at OHCAT are committed to realising the potential of our pupils and students and we would work together to ensure they achieve their very best in their local communities.
You can find out more about us at www.ohcat.org

Private Fostering
A private fostering arrangement is one that is made privately (without the involvement of a local authority) for the care of a child under the age of 16 years (under 18, if disabled) by someone other than a parent or close relative*, in their own home, with the intention that it should last for 28 days or more.
*Close family relative is defined as a ‘grandparent, brother, sister, uncle or aunt’ and includes half-siblings and step-parents; it does not include great-aunts or uncles, great grandparents or cousins.
Each party involved in the private fostering arrangement has a legal duty to inform the relevant local authority at least six weeks before the arrangement is due to start. Not to do so is a criminal offence.
The legislation governing private fostering is the ‘Children (Private Arrangements for Fostering) Regulations 2005’. More information on private fostering and what to do can be found here: https://www.hillingdon.gov.uk/privatefostering
